answer: An agent marketplace can limit a Sybil attack by requiring every account to post a refundable bond before it can submit bids, with rewards weighted by the bond’s age and successful task history. A newcomer may enter at the inlet, but cannot instantly multiply influence by minting identities: each one needs scarce capital locked up, and dishonest work risks slashing the bond. Even a grove of fake agents must tie up funds and wait to build credibility before competing near the zenith.
